questions.prompt: `isLoading` is a signal that is `false`. What does the feed show?

context.label: feed.component.ts

options.text: Always the spinner, never the posts

questions.explanation: A signal is a function, so `isLoading` without `()` is always truthy. Read a signal by calling it: `@if (isLoading())`.

questions.prompt: The header shows the text "user.username" instead of the name. Click the buggy line.

context.label: avatar.component.ts

questions.explanation: Without square brackets, `username="user.username"` passes the literal string. To pass the value of an expression, bind it: `[username]="user.username"`.

questions.prompt: Clicking the heart does nothing, and there is no error. Click the buggy line.

context.label: like-button.component.ts

questions.explanation: `(click)="like"` only refers to the method, it never calls it. Event bindings run a statement, so write `(click)="like()"`. Recent Angular versions can also warn about this at build time.

questions.prompt: What happens when this component is created?

code.label: post-card.component.ts

options.text: It throws an error: a required input has no value yet in the constructor
It works: required inputs are set before the constructor runs

questions.explanation: Inputs are set after the component is created. Reading a required input in the constructor throws (NG0950). Derive the value instead: `readonly likeCount = computed(() => this.post().likes);`.

questions.prompt: The avatar image is rendered by `<app-avatar>`, inside the post header. Does the `.avatar-image` rule in the post header's SCSS apply to it?

options.text: Only if the rule is moved outside `:host`
No. Component styles only reach elements in the component's own template. Style the image in `avatar.component.scss`, or style `.post-avatar` from here

questions.explanation: With Angular's default view encapsulation, a component's styles apply only to its own template. The `<app-avatar>` element itself (`.post-avatar`) is in this template, but the image inside it isn't.

questions.prompt: The action buttons passed to the card never show up. Click the buggy line.
questions.explanation: `select` matches a CSS selector against the projected content. The div has the class `actions`, not `post-actions`, so nothing matches and it isn't shown. With no default `<ng-content />` slot, unmatched content disappears.

options.text: The build fails: `@for` needs a `track` expression
It works, but Angular re-renders every comment on each change

questions.explanation: `track` is required in `@for`. Track something unique and stable: `@for (comment of comments(); track comment.id)`.

questions.prompt: What happens when you build this component?

context.label: post-header.component.ts

options.text: The build fails: no pipe named `date` is available here
It builds, and the date shows as an ISO string
It builds: built-in pipes are available everywhere

questions.explanation: A standalone component only has what its `imports` array lists. Add `DatePipe` to `imports`.
